sampling_model.design: A binary randomized instrument \(Z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), independent of the saturated response type.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(Z_i,X_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), are independent and identically distributed draws from \(P\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(X\) takes values in finite \(\mathcal E\); categories in \(T\) share well-defined outcomes across instrument arms and categories in \(U\) impose no cross-arm outcome restriction.
sampling_model.overlap: Only instrument-arm positivity \(0<\rho<1\) is required; exposure cells may have probability zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All observable inputs are finite arm-cell probabilities estimated by empirical conditional frequencies; the finite-sample theorem does not estimate a smooth nuisance function.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For binary instrument, exposure, and outcome, the sharp average-effect interval is the maximum and minimum of eight affine response-function expressions.
Result 1 gives the classical eight-piece bounds for two well-defining target levels plus one merged potentially ill-defining remainder.
Equations (3)--(4) give ten sharp lower and upper expressions for a binary instrument and three well-defining exposure levels.
Theorem 1 gives the same joint potential-outcome and observed-law image for the five categorical instrumental-variable models in Table 2.
The five full-category models have the same observed-law image, which excludes some laws admitted when exclusion is imposed only on selected categories.
Theorem 17 characterizes the observable binary-instrument, binary-outcome, arbitrary-exposure model under full exclusion by instrumental inequalities.
For a finite response-function class, dual vertex enumeration yields valid and tight symbolic bounds for linear causal queries.
A multinomial Kullback--Leibler confidence region gives simultaneous finite-sample coverage for linear functionals of the fully valid categorical-IV counterfactual law.
Identification gains for binary average-effect bounds can be decomposed into contributions from instrument information and model features.

body.tldr: With a randomized binary instrument, binary outcome, and arbitrary finite categorical exposure, exclusion and consistency may be credible only on a declared trusted subset containing the two target categories. The sharp pairwise-effect interval is governed by one two-diagonal capacity: each endpoint evaluates eight baseline affine pieces and exactly two pieces per trusted nuisance category, with finite laws attaining both endpoints. Trust is nested by an explicit response-law restriction map, and separate positive-cell witnesses show strict observed-law enlargement from selected trust and strict identified-set tightening from adding trust. Comparator scope is exact: Balke--Pearl is recovered literally only for a binary exposure; a merged wholly untrusted remainder is Gabriel--Sachs--Sjolander Result 1; full trust with three categories gives their ten terms; and arbitrary finite full trust is Song--Guo--Chan--Richardson model M1, with the pairwise interval transferring to models M2 through M5 by their equal-image theorem. Finite-sample whole-set coverage remains valid at ties and zero cells.

project_justification.gap: Balke and Pearl give the literal binary-exposure envelope. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander give both the two-target result with one merged wholly untrusted remainder and the ten-term fully trusted ternary formulas. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson characterize arbitrary finite categorical exposure under full trust and prove that five IV formulations have the same joint potential-outcome and observed-law image, but leave scalar pairwise endpoints to generic optimization. What is missing is an arbitrary-finite sharp scalar envelope when trust is category selective, together with an exact nesting map and strict witnesses on the common observed-law domain.
project_justification.niche: Applied adherence studies often have two interventionally meaningful target categories, several intermediate categories for which exclusion may be separately defensible, and residual categories for which no cross-instrument outcome equality is credible. That structure is neither a binary exposure model nor a fully exclusion-valid categorical model.
project_justification.fill: The two-diagonal transport reduction supplies the sharp linear-size envelope and finite endpoint laws for the mixed-trust model. The response-law restriction map proves that enlarging trust nests both compatibility classes and identified sets; the separation and gain tables make both inclusions strict in the appropriate sense. Exact reductions recover Balke--Pearl only on a genuinely binary alphabet, Gabriel's merged-remainder and ternary formulas in their stated scopes, and Song's five equal images under arbitrary finite full trust.

body.related_work: Balke and Pearl derive eight sharp affine average-effect expressions for binary instrument, binary exposure, and binary outcome; the present formula is called literally Balke--Pearl only when the exposure alphabet has two elements. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjolander Result 1 treats two well-defining target levels plus one merged potentially ill-defining remainder and recovers those eight expressions, while their equations (3)--(4) give ten sharp expressions per endpoint for three well-defining exposure levels. These are the faithful published reductions of the selected-trust formula. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjolander, and Gabriel provide general symbolic primal--dual machinery for finite response-function models; that machinery informs certification but is not the linear-size envelope proved here. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson characterize arbitrary categorical IV models under full trust. Their model M1 coincides with this paper's full-trust response-law image, and their Theorem 1 proves equality of the joint potential-outcome and observed-law images of models M1 through M5, so the sharp pairwise interval transfers exactly to all five formulations. Bhadane, Mooij, Boeken, and Zoeter Theorem 17 gives the observed full-exclusion compatibility characterization for binary instrument and outcome with arbitrary finite exposure. The cell-sum inequality violated by the separation family is attributed to that observed-model result and also follows directly because the two relevant full-exclusion factual events are disjoint. That family is selected-trust compatible on a positive-cell neighborhood but not full-trust representable, whereas the separate full-trust-compatible gain table shows strict identified-set tightening after trusting the intermediate category. VanderWeele and Hernan explain why coarse labels may hide treatment versions, and Marshall studies bias from coarsening; they motivate the distinction between a trusted refinement and a wholly untrusted split or merge. Zhang, Frazier, Poskitt, and Zhao analyze identification gains for binary average-effect bounds; the categorywise active-face update here is a corollary of the sharp envelope. Du Toit and collaborators supply the LEAP adherence application in which separately justified intermediate consumption categories may or may not change the low-versus-high interval.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The phrase \(8+2|T\setminus\{a,b\}|\) denotes a complete affine evaluation list for each endpoint, not an assertion that every listed term is an irredundant facet on every lower-dimensional support stratum. Formula remark: a wholly untrusted refinement obeys \(L_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=L_T(p)\) and \(U_{\widetilde T}(\widetilde p)=U_T(p)\); push a factual coupling forward through \(g\), and lift it by arbitrary disintegration within each untrusted fiber. Implementation note: compute the eight baseline faces, scan \(c\in T\setminus\{a,b\}\), update the lower maximum and upper minimum with the two category faces, and retain ties; this uses \(O(|\mathcal E|)\) arithmetic and \(O(1)\) auxiliary memory beyond the input and active-face output. These are formula and implementation consequences, not independent research targets. Producing a full attaining transport by generic augmenting paths is claimed only to terminate in finite polynomial time.
body.honest_scope: The sole identification kernel is the sharp-envelope theorem with its transport completion and finite endpoint-attaining laws. The perturbation-stable non-representability family and the separate open strict-gain region provide the load-bearing comparison with the full-exclusion model of Song et al.; the Hoeffding whole-set theorem supplies finite-sample coverage. The categorywise trust update is a one-line corollary, wholly untrusted refinement is a formula remark, and one-pass evaluation is an implementation note. The bounded computations are diagnostic evidence: the supplied checker reported agreement across \(840\) response-law linear programs, \(9{,}648\) exact rational endpoint constructions, and the exact LEAP interval \([-5073/31720,10/61]\); the denominator-three early-kill enumeration reported \(109{,}440\) exact endpoint constructions. These checks are not theorem premises. The Outlook question remains open over triangular arrays without cell, face-gap, or face-variance floors, while its strict precision comparison is restricted to nonempty compact regular classes. No monotonicity, exposure ordering, instrument relevance, exposure-cell positivity, or clinical justification of any trusted LEAP category is claimed.
